## <a id="pkg-overview"></a>Overview

Package hottytest is a hotty host that runs inside a test. The program under test reads from it and writes to it as it would a terminal; the test then looks at what the program showed, and plays the user.

```go
h := hottytest.New(t)
run(hottyterm.New(h, h, "tool", h.TermSize, nil)) // the program under test; or tea.WithInput(h), …
card := h.Surface("tool-card")
card.TextOf("status")                         // what it shows
h.Click("tool-card", "retry")                 // what the user does
h.Key("Tab")                                  // keys, as SPEC §10.2 has a host take them
```

The host keeps every surface's document as the program's commands leave it, with the delta operations and the morph of SPEC §6, and answers each command as SPEC §3.6 has hosts do. It passes the hotty conformance vectors that need no layout: it skips the ones marked scroll, steps, drop and view, and those for features it lacks (SDK.md §4.4). It lays nothing out and draws no pixels: a placement with auto rows gets an estimate (AutoRows), nothing in it scrolls, and a test says where in an element a pointer is (DragStartStep).

A placement made on the alternate screen goes with it, and so does its surface (SPEC §5.4). A full reset (RIS) deletes every surface.

It keeps each control's rev and each text field's selection, focused or not, as a=field reads them (SPEC §6.4; Surface.Rev, Surface.Selection), takes a=field as a host does, and sends the rev in input and change and the selection in input and caret (data-on~=caret). Its text fields keep no history of their edits: it does not claim the undo feature.

It keeps the touch areas the program names (a=touch, SPEC §9.6) for each screen, as a host does, and checks them as one does (TouchAreas); no finger reaches them.

It also answers the queries terminals answer: Primary Device Attributes, the cursor's position, the background colour, and, when asked to (KittyGraphics), the kitty graphics query. It keeps the cells the program printed, as rows (Screen) and as the lines it wrote (Lines), and where it left the cursor (Cursor).

A Host made with Text is a terminal that is not a hotty host: the program's commands get no answer, as in any other terminal.

A Host made with NoTerminal is a multiplexer running the program's pane with no terminal attached: it answers ENOTERM to a placement with auto rows, and lays the surfaces out when AttachTerminal attaches one (SPEC §5.2).

Unless Lenient, a program that breaks the protocol fails the test: a malformed command, one the host refuses as invalid (EINVAL), or a hotty command other than the query sent to a terminal that is not a host.

## <a id="Body"></a>func Body

```go
func Body(js string) []byte
```

Body is a body written as JSON, as the msgpack a host sends (SPEC §3.3): a number with a fraction or an exponent is a float, any other an int, as the conformance vectors write them, and a map keeps its keys in the order written. It is for a test that makes up what a host says, such as Body(\`{"code":"ENOENT"}\`) in an error reply, or what a program says, such as a delta's ops. It panics when js is not JSON.

## <a id="DefaultCaps"></a>func DefaultCaps

```go
func DefaultCaps() hotty.Caps
```

DefaultCaps are the capabilities a Host reports unless Caps says otherwise. Its features are the ones it can honour: it lays nothing out, so it has no passthrough, but it hears where the pointer is (hover), counts clicks (count, DoubleClick) and records the menu a program shows (menu, Menu).

### <a id="New"></a>func New

```go
func New(tb testing.TB, opts ...Option) *Host
```

New makes a host for a test, closed when the test ends. tb may be nil outside a test: then nothing fails, and Errors lists what would have.

### <a id="Host.AttachTerminal"></a>func (*Host) AttachTerminal

```go
func (h *Host) AttachTerminal()
```

AttachTerminal attaches a terminal to the pane of a host made with NoTerminal, or one DetachTerminal left without. The terminal lays every surface out: a placement answered ENOTERM gets its rows, and one with f=1 hears them as fit, as it does any rows that differ from the ones it last heard (SPEC §5.2).

### <a id="Host.BecomeHost"></a>func (*Host) BecomeHost

```go
func (h *Host) BecomeHost()
```

BecomeHost makes a terminal made with Text a hotty host from now on, as a multiplexer becomes one when a terminal that is a host attaches to the program's pane: it answers the last query the program sent, if that one asked for a late answer (late=1, SPEC §4) and was not withdrawn or reset since, and every command after.

### <a id="Host.Blur"></a>func (*Host) Blur

```go
func (h *Host) Blur(surface string) error
```

Blur takes the keyboard from a surface, as a click elsewhere does: the control being edited commits (change), then blur.

### <a id="Host.Buffered"></a>func (*Host) Buffered

```go
func (h *Host) Buffered() int
```

Buffered is how many bytes the host has sent that the program has not read: a test that hands a program its input itself, a Bubble Tea model's Update say, reads that much without blocking.

### <a id="Host.Change"></a>func (*Host) Change

```go
func (h *Host) Change(f func(c *hotty.Caps))
```

Change changes the capabilities the host reports, as the terminal does when the user changes its font, theme or settings, or when a multiplexer's program moves to another viewer's host (SPEC §4): f is given a copy to change. The program, if it asked, then hears caps with every field that differs from what it last heard (SPEC §9), the empty value for one that became absent. A new scale alone says nothing: a zoom is not told (SPEC §4). A new cell size lays the documents out again, so a surface that asked for fit may hear it.

### <a id="Host.Check"></a>func (*Host) Check

```go
func (h *Host) Check(surface, id string, on bool) error
```

Check sets a checkbox, or chooses a radio button (on must then be true), as the user does: change comes at once.

### <a id="Host.Choose"></a>func (*Host) Choose

```go
func (h *Host) Choose(surface, id, value string) error
```

Choose picks an option of a select by its value, as from its list: input (with data-on~=input) and change come at once.

### <a id="Host.Click"></a>func (*Host) Click

```go
func (h *Host) Click(surface, id string, keys ...string) error
```

Click clicks the element with an id, as the user does (SPEC §9): a press first, if the placement asks for presses; the keyboard, if the element takes focus, or else back to the terminal from the surface that had it (blur, SPEC §10.1); then click, reported by the nearest element from it outward that reports clicks, if that has an id. A link reports its href, and a hyperlink (target=\_blank) is opened by the terminal and reports nothing (Opened). A submit button then submits its form.

keys are the modifier keys held ("shift", "ctrl", "alt", "super"); the click carries those held at its release (SPEC §9). A press with Alt is the program's own gesture (SPEC §9.2): the surface hears nothing of it, and the pointer is out of its window.

On a detached surface the click does what is local and reports nothing: ErrDetached.

```go
func (h *Host) ClickLink(surface, href string, keys ...string) error
```

ClickLink clicks the first link in a surface whose href is href, as written in the document: for links with no id, such as a manual page's references. It is Click on that link.

### <a id="Host.DragEnd"></a>func (*Host) DragEnd

```go
func (h *Host) DragEnd(id string, c, r int, keys ...string) error
```

DragEnd releases the button of the drag in progress over the element with an id, or none (""), at the surface's cell c, r (SPEC §9.1): dragend, its t as DragMove's. A drag that ends on the element it began on is also that element's click, after dragend, if it reports clicks: the nearest element with an id and drag in its data-on, from the one named outward, is the one it began on, whatever t is.


```go

```

DragEndStep is DragEnd with the pointer at step x, y of the element the drag began on (DragStartStep).

### <a id="Host.DragMove"></a>func (*Host) DragMove

```go
func (h *Host) DragMove(id string, c, r int, keys ...string) error
```

DragMove moves the pointer of the drag in progress onto the element with an id in the drag's surface, or onto none ("": a gap, another surface, the cells, outside the window), at the surface's cell c, r (SPEC §9.1). It reports drag when the element under the pointer changes: t, the nearest one with an id and drag in its data-on (or drop), from it outward, or empty; while that is empty, when the cell changes instead. In a t with data-steps the pointer stays at the step it was at in t, or 0 in a new one (DragOver).

### <a id="Host.DragMoveStep"></a>func (*Host) DragMoveStep

```go
func (h *Host) DragMoveStep(id string, c, r, x, y int, keys ...string) error
```

DragMoveStep is DragMove with the pointer at step x, y of the element the drag began on, wherever the pointer is (DragStartStep). It also reports drag when the step changes.

### <a id="Host.DragOver"></a>func (*Host) DragOver

```go
func (h *Host) DragOver(id string, c, r, tx, ty int, keys ...string) error
```

DragOver is DragMove with the pointer at step tx, ty of t, for a t with drop in its data-on and data-steps (SPEC §9.1): a row with "0 1" is split in halves, a folder with "0 2" into before, into and after. The host lays nothing out, so the test says where in t the pointer is; a step past t's count is clamped to it, and one along an axis t does not count is ignored. It also reports drag when that step changes.

### <a id="Host.DragStart"></a>func (*Host) DragStart

```go
func (h *Host) DragStart(surface, id string, c, r int, keys ...string) error
```

DragStart presses a mouse's primary button on the element with an id and starts a drag (SPEC §9.1), at the surface's cell c, r, with the modifier keys held ("shift", "ctrl", "alt", "super"). The press is a press like any other: press first, if the placement asks for presses; then dragstart, from the nearest element from it outward with drag in its data-on; then the keyboard, as a click moves it. ErrNoReport, and no drag, if no element opts in or the one that does has no id.

The host lays nothing out, so a test names what is under the pointer: DragMove for each element or cell crossed, then DragEnd.

### <a id="Host.DragStartStep"></a>func (*Host) DragStartStep

```go
func (h *Host) DragStartStep(surface, id string, c, r, x, y int, keys ...string) error
```

DragStartStep is DragStart on an element with data-steps (SPEC §9.1), with the pointer at step x, y of it. The host lays nothing out, so the test says where in the element the pointer is; a step past the element's count is clamped to it, and one along an axis it does not count is ignored.

### <a id="Host.Fill"></a>func (*Host) Fill

```go
func (h *Host) Fill(surface, id, text string) error
```

Fill types text into a text control, as the user does: the surface takes the keyboard there (a focus event, if it did not have it), the control's value becomes text (an input event, with data-on~=input), the caret goes to its end with nothing selected, and the change is committed when focus leaves it (Blur, another control, Submit).

### <a id="Host.Forget"></a>func (*Host) Forget

```go
func (h *Host) Forget()
```

Forget drops every surface and resource behind the program's back, as a host does that restarts behind a relay: the program is not told, and finds out from the ENOENT its next placement gets. The screen stays as it is.

### <a id="Host.Hover"></a>func (*Host) Hover

```go
func (h *Host) Hover(surface, id string, c, r int) error
```

Hover moves the pointer onto a placed surface, over the element with an id (or "" for a point over nothing with an id), at the surface's cell c, r. The surface the pointer was on is left first. A placement made with Hover hears hover when the element differs from what it heard last; moves within an element send nothing.

The host lays nothing out, so a test names what is under the pointer, as for drags.

```go
func (h *Host) Invalid() int
```

Invalid counts the malformed messages the program sent.

### <a id="Host.Key"></a>func (*Host) Key

```go
func (h *Host) Key(key string) (used bool)
```

Key types a key as the user does, and does with it what SPEC §10.2 has a host do while a surface has the keyboard. The key is named as SPEC §10.4 names it, as myelin key names do: its modifiers, joined by "+", and a character, a physical key or a modifier key: "a", "shift+a", "space", "enter", "tab", "shift+tab", "backspace", "arrow\_down", "escape", "ctrl+s". A press has one name here, as the program would read it (SPEC §10.4): a binding of a physical key (ctrl+key\_w) holds only where the test gives that name. A name that does not parse is no key; the program gets nothing of it.

tab and shift+tab move focus from the focused element to the next or the previous of the surface's focusable elements in tree order, those with a negative tabindex and those in an inert subtree left out (an element focused with a negative tabindex is where they start from); past the last, or before the first, the surface loses the keyboard (blur). A text field (a text-like input, a textarea) does what its keymap says (hotty.Resolve, with the data-keys of the elements from the root to it): it edits its value at a caret and a selection this host keeps, as hottyedit.Field does, with an input event for each edit (data-on~=input), each one more rev, and a caret event for each move and each edit no input event reports (data-on~=caret); a move whose key has shift selects (hotty.Keymap.Selects), select-all selects the value, characters type in place of the selection, and submit commits the value and submits its form.

Any other element has a keymap too, read the same way but with no default keymap (hotty.Keymap.Program): a key it binds to program reaches the program, and its other bindings do nothing. This host does not scroll, so a key bound to a scroll action goes on as if the keymap did not bind it (SPEC §10.2). The element takes the other keys of its row of the table, unmodified or with shift only:

  - a button, a link, a summary: space and enter click it (another element that reports clicks, data-on~=click, uses no keys);
  - a checkbox or a radio button: space checks it, enter submits its form;
  - a date or time input: the keys a text input's default keymap binds, and characters; the arrows up and down and the page keys are used;
  - a select: the arrows, home and end pick an option, the page keys as far as home and end, a character the next option its label starts, past disabled ones; a pick sends input (with data-on~=input) and change at once. space and enter do nothing: this host shows no list.

With no element focused there is no keymap: the data-keys of the document are not read, and every key but tab is the program's.

Every other key reaches the program, as typed (Type) when it has a terminal encoding here: characters, enter, tab, escape, backspace, the arrows and the editing keys, and ctrl or alt with a character. So does every key while no surface has the keyboard. used reports whether a surface used the key.

```go
func (h *Host) Lines() []string
```

Lines is the screen's text as the program wrote its lines: Screen, with each row that a line went on to when it was wider than the terminal (autowrap) joined to the row before it. A row erased whole starts a line of its own.

```go
func (h *Host) Menu() *hotty.MenuTree
```

Menu is the menu the program keeps on the screen it is on (a=menu, SPEC §10.7), nil when it has none: the program sent none or an empty a=menu, or it was the alternate screen's and the program left it, or a reset. A host without the feature menu answers a=menu EINVAL.

### <a id="Host.Opened"></a>func (*Host) Opened

```go
func (h *Host) Opened() []string
```

Opened are the hyperlinks the user opened (target=\_blank), which the terminal opens itself and never reports (SPEC §9).

### <a id="Host.Output"></a>func (*Host) Output

```go
func (h *Host) Output() string
```

Output is every byte the program wrote.

### <a id="Host.Pick"></a>func (*Host) Pick

```go
func (h *Host) Pick(name string) bool
```

Pick picks the item of the program's menu named name, as a multiplexer's palette or an agent would (SPEC §10.7): the program hears a command event with that name. The first item so named, depth first, is the one. It sends nothing, and reports false, for an item that is not enabled, a name no item has, or no menu.

### <a id="Host.Prefix"></a>func (*Host) Prefix

```go
func (h *Host) Prefix() string
```

Prefix is the surface whose keys all reach the program since a key its keymap binds to prefix (SPEC §10.5), until the program sends a=focus or a=blur, the surface loses the keyboard, or the user focuses an element of it with a press; "" when none.

### <a id="Host.Press"></a>func (*Host) Press

```go
func (h *Host) Press(surface, id string, keys ...string) error
```

Press presses the element with an id, or empty space ("") (SPEC §9): reported only on a placement made with Placement.Press, as the id of the nearest element with one.

### <a id="Host.Read"></a>func (*Host) Read

```go
func (h *Host) Read(p []byte) (int, error)
```

Read is the program's input: answers, events and keys, as a terminal sends them. It blocks until there is some, or the host is closed.

### <a id="Host.Replies"></a>func (*Host) Replies

```go
func (h *Host) Replies() []hotty.Message
```

Replies are the replies the host sent, in order.

### <a id="Host.Resource"></a>func (*Host) Resource

```go
func (h *Host) Resource(id string) (mime string, data []byte, ok bool)
```

Resource is a resource the program stored (SPEC §7.1).

### <a id="Host.Screen"></a>func (*Host) Screen

```go
func (h *Host) Screen() string
```

Screen is the cells the program printed, a line a row, without colours: what is left after carriage returns, cursor moves, erases and scrolls. It is the main screen, its scrollback first, or the alternate screen while the program has it on. Surfaces are not drawn in it; the rows a placement covered are blank.

### <a id="Host.Shown"></a>func (*Host) Shown

```go
func (h *Host) Shown() []hotty.MenuItem
```

Shown is the level of the menu that the host shows (a=menu:show=1, SPEC §10.7): the items of the group the program's keys reach that have a key, in order. It is nil when no level shows: the program showed none or hid it, or the user's Escape or a key the level does not list hid it, or the keys reach no group, or no item there has a key.

### <a id="Host.Submit"></a>func (*Host) Submit

```go
func (h *Host) Submit(surface, id string) error
```

Submit submits a form, as Enter in one of its fields does: id is the form's, or a control's in it. The control being edited commits first. A form without an id reports nothing.

### <a id="Host.Surface"></a>func (*Host) Surface

```go
func (h *Host) Surface(name string) *Surface
```

Surface is the surface of a name, nil when there is none.

### <a id="Host.Surfaces"></a>func (*Host) Surfaces

```go
func (h *Host) Surfaces() []*Surface
```

Surfaces are the surfaces there are, in the order they were created.

### <a id="Host.TermSize"></a>func (*Host) TermSize

```go
func (h *Host) TermSize() (cols, rows int)
```

TermSize is the terminal's size (Size), as hottyterm.New takes it.

### <a id="Host.TouchAreas"></a>func (*Host) TouchAreas

```go
func (h *Host) TouchAreas() []hotty.TouchArea
```

TouchAreas are the touch areas the program keeps on the screen it is on (a=touch, SPEC §9.6), in the order it listed them: nil when it has none. It sent none, or an a=touch with no areas, or they were the alternate screen's and the program left it, or a reset dropped them. An a=touch whose body is no map of areas is EINVAL, and leaves the areas as they were.

### <a id="Host.Type"></a>func (*Host) Type

```go
func (h *Host) Type(keys string)
```

Type sends text to the program as keys typed: "q", "\\r" for Enter, "\\x03" for Ctrl-C, "\\x1b" for Escape.

### <a id="Host.Unhover"></a>func (*Host) Unhover

```go
func (h *Host) Unhover()
```

Unhover takes the pointer off the surface it is on: onto the cells, or out of the terminal's window. A placement made with Hover hears it is out.

### <a id="Host.Write"></a>func (*Host) Write

```go
func (h *Host) Write(p []byte) (int, error)
```

Write is the program's output. It is parsed as it comes: hotty commands are carried out and answered, the terminal's queries answered, and the rest kept as cells (Screen). It never fails.

## <a id="Option"></a>type Option

```go
type Option func(*Host)
```

Option configures a Host.

### <a id="AutoRows"></a>func AutoRows

```go
func AutoRows(f func(s *Surface, cols int) int) Option
```

AutoRows sets how many rows a placement with auto rows gets, for its surface laid out cols wide. The default counts the body's lines of text and its block elements.

### <a id="Caps"></a>func Caps

```go
func Caps(c hotty.Caps) Option
```

Caps sets the capabilities the host reports. Fields left zero keep the defaults (DefaultCaps). Features replace the default list: a test that wants a host without hover or menus names the ones it has.

### <a id="KittyGraphics"></a>func KittyGraphics

```go
func KittyGraphics() Option
```

KittyGraphics makes the terminal answer the kitty graphics query, as one that shows images does.

### <a id="Lenient"></a>func Lenient

```go
func Lenient() Option
```

Lenient keeps protocol errors from failing the test; Errors still lists them.

### <a id="NoTerminal"></a>func NoTerminal

```go
func NoTerminal() Option
```

NoTerminal makes the host a multiplexer running the program's pane with no terminal attached, until AttachTerminal (SPEC §5.2). It has nothing to lay a document out with: a placement with auto rows is made, and answered ENOTERM where its rows would be; the cursor stays where it was, below rows nobody knows yet; and no placement hears fit.

### <a id="Size"></a>func Size

```go
func Size(cols, rows int) Option
```

Size sets the terminal's size in cells; 80×24 by default.

### <a id="Text"></a>func Text

```go
func Text() Option
```

Text makes the host a terminal that is not a hotty host: it answers DA1 and the cursor's position, and ignores hotty, until BecomeHost.

## <a id="Surface"></a>type Surface

```go
type Surface struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Surface is one surface the program made: its document, as the program's commands left it, and its placement.

### <a id="Surface.At"></a>func (*Surface) At

```go
func (s *Surface) At() (col, row int)
```

At is the cell of the placement's top-left corner: the cursor's, when the program placed it. row is a line of Screen, the scrollback's included, of the screen it was placed on.

### <a id="Surface.Attr"></a>func (*Surface) Attr

```go
func (s *Surface) Attr(id, name string) (string, bool)
```

Attr is an attribute of the element with an id.

### <a id="Surface.Detached"></a>func (*Surface) Detached

```go
func (s *Surface) Detached() bool
```

Detached reports whether the surface is detached (SPEC §5.5).

### <a id="Surface.Element"></a>func (*Surface) Element

```go
func (s *Surface) Element(id string) (e Element, ok bool)
```

Element finds the element with an id. ok is false when there is none.

### <a id="Surface.Fit"></a>func (*Surface) Fit

```go
func (s *Surface) Fit() bool
```

Fit reports whether the program asked for fit events (Placement.Fit).

### <a id="Surface.Focused"></a>func (*Surface) Focused

```go
func (s *Surface) Focused() string
```

Focused is the id of the element that has focus, while the surface has the keyboard; "" otherwise.

### <a id="Surface.HTML"></a>func (*Surface) HTML

```go
func (s *Surface) HTML() string
```

HTML is the document as it is now.

### <a id="Surface.Hover"></a>func (*Surface) Hover

```go
func (s *Surface) Hover() bool
```

Hover reports whether the program asked for hover events (Placement.Hover).

### <a id="Surface.Name"></a>func (*Surface) Name

```go
func (s *Surface) Name() string
```

Name is the surface's name.

### <a id="Surface.Placed"></a>func (*Surface) Placed

```go
func (s *Surface) Placed() bool
```

Placed reports whether the surface is placed: on screen, not hidden.

### <a id="Surface.Placement"></a>func (*Surface) Placement

```go
func (s *Surface) Placement() hotty.Placement
```

Placement is the surface's last placement, as the program sent it; Rows is the rows the host chose when the program asked for auto, 0 while no terminal has laid it out (NoTerminal).

### <a id="Surface.Press"></a>func (*Surface) Press

```go
func (s *Surface) Press() bool
```

Press reports whether the program asked for presses (Placement.Press): the flag belongs to the surface, and holds across placements (SPEC §5.2).

### <a id="Surface.Rev"></a>func (*Surface) Rev

```go
func (s *Surface) Rev(id string) (rev int, ok bool)
```

Rev is a control's revision (SPEC §6.4): 0 when it entered the document, one more for each change the user made to its value or its checked; a radio button's is its group's. ok is false when there is no element with the id, or it is not a control a=field takes.

### <a id="Surface.Selection"></a>func (*Surface) Selection

```go
func (s *Surface) Selection(id string) (anchor, caret int, ok bool)
```

Selection is a text field's selection, focused or not, as a=field counts it (SPEC §6.4): its anchor, then its caret, in bytes of its value; the two are the same when nothing is selected. ok is false when there is no element with the id, or it is not a text field.

### <a id="Surface.Text"></a>func (*Surface) Text

```go
func (s *Surface) Text() string
```

Text is the text of the document's body as a reader sees it, roughly: block elements apart, runs of whitespace one space, styles and scripts left out.

### <a id="Surface.TextOf"></a>func (*Surface) TextOf

```go
func (s *Surface) TextOf(id string) string
```

TextOf is the text of the element with an id, "" when there is none.

### <a id="Surface.Value"></a>func (*Surface) Value

```go
func (s *Surface) Value(id string) (string, bool)
```

Value is a control's current value: what the program set, or the user typed (Fill). For a checkbox or radio button, "true" or "false".

### <a id="Surface.Var"></a>func (*Surface) Var

```go
func (s *Surface) Var(id, name string) (string, bool)
```

Var is the custom property --name set on the element with an id, by the document's style attribute or a var delta.
